chris_account_exec: Hey team — ACME wants to run the Private POC next Wed. They prefer PrivateLink over peering. Security is asking for a precise list of firewall exceptions, egress IPs, and any required subnet sizes. Can SRE confirm what's needed for a smooth POC? @amy_sales @nick_sre

amy_sales: FYI they also asked if we need any inbound rules on their side or if everything is outbound from their VPC. They want this in writing for their security questionnaire. :pray:

nick_sre: Short version: PrivateLink (interface VPC endpoints) is the cleanest for POC — no peering, no route table changes beyond the ENI created by the endpoint. For PrivateLink we need the customer to create an Interface VPC Endpoint to our service (we provide the service name) and allow the endpoint's security group to reach the subnets you want to use. Minimal firewall rules on their side: outbound TCP 443 to the endpoint, and allow traffic from the endpoint SG to the app subnets.

Longer details below.

- If they insist on VPC Peering: require route table entries, and if their subnets are private behind a NAT you must ensure NAT allows connections to our control plane IPs. Peering does not traverse NAT; peered traffic is direct.
- We do not publish fixed public egress IPs for hosted control plane traffic. For short POCs, PrivateLink avoids public egress entirely.

Example SG egress (on customer side) to allow connection to our interface endpoint: ```
Type    Protocol  Port Range  Destination
Egress  TCP       443         vpce-<id> (Interface endpoint)
```

Example SG on endpoint to allow traffic to app subnets: ```
Type    Protocol  Port Range  Destination
Ingress TCP       443         10.0.0.0/24   # customer's app subnet
```

Also: if they want to reach S3 for model artifacts/logs, either use a S3 Gateway endpoint (recommended) or allow outbound 443 to S3 endpoints.

Last: we can enable mTLS for control plane auth on Private deployments if they require cert-based mutual TLS — we'll need their CA or to provision certs during onboarding.

pooja_se: A few sec-qa items to add to the writeup for their questionnaire:
- We support encryption in transit (TLS 1.2+) and at rest (KMS).
- For PrivateLink POC we need: customer AWS account ID, VPC ID, CIDR(s) for the subnets you want to use, preferred AZs, and the security contact (email).
- Subnet sizing: endpoint ENIs are small but recommend at least a /24 per AZ to avoid exhaustion during scale tests.
- If they require IP allowlists: for PrivateLink the allowed peers will be the endpoint ENI IPs (we'll provide after endpoint creation).

amy_sales: Great. Can we also give them a short line on cost? They asked if PrivateLink adds extra fees to the POC.

nick_sre: PrivateLink itself incurs AWS endpoint charges on their bill. Redwood doesn't charge extra for the interface endpoint for a short POC — if they move to a Private deployment there is the standard Private licensing + infra. For Dedicated/Reserved it's a different quote. For the POC we typically cover 2 weeks of usage under evaluation credits; network egress (if they go public) may be billed by cloud provider to their account.

deploy-bot: POC token created: poc-ACME-2026-03. Expires in 72h. :robot_face:

chris_account_exec: Perfect — can someone draft a 1-page connectivity checklist I can send to their security team? I'll pull the account/VPC info once they confirm.

nick_sre: I'll draft it — short checklist + snippet for SGs + what we need from them. Putting a note: if they want static egress IPs, the options are (1) customer NAT with Elastic IPs, (2) transit/peering via a transit gateway we coordinate with (requires routing changes), or (3) we deploy in their VPC for fully private infra (enterprise-only, separate quote).

pooja_se: I'll add the mTLS and KMS lines into the checklist.

amy_sales: Thanks — if possible include a one-liner they can paste into their security questionnaire about no public data exposure during PrivateLink POC. :thumbsup:

nick_sre: Will do. ETA: I'll drop the checklist here by EOD PST today.

chris_account_exec: Awesome, appreciate it. I'll ping ACME network contact once checklist is ready.
